r4a-envelope-not-mean.title: Envelope (p10) not mean/median onset -- THE #1 check
r4a-envelope-not-mean.imperative: Verify the pre-authored TestEnvelopeNotMean test genuinely proves the produced braking-zone onset equals the p10 (BRAKING_ONSET_QUANTILE) crossing of brake_active_frac and is strictly upstream (earlier distance) of the 0.5/mean crossing -- quote the assertion. Confirm tiling.py's code (_grid_type_array) computes onset by comparing brake_active_frac against the imported BRAKING_ONSET_QUANTILE directly, never a mean()/median() call or any other central-tendency statistic. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4a-envelope-not-mean.finding: CONFIRMED, the #1 check. Code: _grid_type_array's onset search is 'for j in range(prev_corner_end, c_start): if ref.brake_active_frac[j] >= BRAKING_ONSET_QUANTILE: onset_idx = j; break' -- a direct threshold-crossing comparison against the imported p10 constant, first (most-upstream) qualifying index wins. grep -n 'np.mean|np.median|\.mean\(|\.median\(' tiling.py -> zero matches: no mean/median call anywhere in the file. Test proof (TestEnvelopeNotMean.test_p10_onset_is_earlier_than_mean_crossing): fixture is bimodal -- brake_active_frac=0.15 (>p10=0.10, <0.5) from idx 60, rising to 0.6 (>0.5) only from idx 75; a fixture sanity assert first proves 'expected_p10_onset_boundary < would_be_mean_onset_boundary' (so the test cannot vacuously pass on a degenerate fixture where the two coincide). The load-bearing assertions then quote-for-quote: 'assert produced_onset == pytest.approx(expected_p10_onset_boundary), f"braking-zone onset must equal the p10 envelope crossing ({expected_p10_onset_boundary}), got {produced_onset}"' and 'assert produced_onset < would_be_mean_onset_boundary, "the p10 envelope onset must be STRICTLY upstream (earlier, smaller distance) of the 0.5/mean crossing -- a mean onset would sit inside the real braking zone and miss the early brakers..."'. Both assertions passed (9/9 green, reproduced independently). This genuinely proves onset == the p10 crossing AND strictly precedes the 0.5 crossing -- not a coincidental pass on a fixture where the two thresholds happen to land on the same index.

r4c-complete-partition.title: Complete contiguous partition, coverage recomputed
r4c-complete-partition.imperative: Confirm boundaries_m is strictly increasing, starts at 0.0, ends at lap_length_m, and that TestCompleteness independently recomputes per-grid-station coverage (not just checking the four scalar invariants) to prove no gap/overlap. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4c-complete-partition.finding: Confirmed. Tiling.__post_init__ mechanically enforces b[0]/b[-1] shape via len(t)==len(b)-1 and 'np.all(np.diff(b) > 0.0)' (strictly increasing, so no zero-length or overlapping segment can exist by construction). TestCompleteness.test_partition_invariants_and_coverage goes beyond the four scalars: it independently builds expected_grid_type (from the SAME rule the test author derived, NOT by calling _grid_type_array), then uses np.searchsorted(b, ref.distance_m, side='right')-1 to map every one of the 100 grid stations back to its produced segment, and asserts np.testing.assert_array_equal(recovered, expected_grid_type) across the WHOLE array -- a genuine per-point coverage recomputation, not a spot check. Reproduced (test passed, part of the 9/9 run). _group_into_segments only emits a boundary when grid_type[i] != current (line 141), so adjacent same-type stations always merge into one segment -- no possibility of a spurious zero-content boundary. The closing segment (last grid station -> lap_length_m) is correctly attributed to that last station's own type, matching SegmentMap's own boundaries_m[-1]==lap_length_m convention per the docstring.
